plan.melodySummary: The 'Ode to Joy' theme travels through the ensemble beginning warmly in the Clarinet, passing to Violin 1 for the soaring restatements, dipping into the Cello and French Horn for lyrical contrast, and returning to the massed violins for the triumphant climax. The dynamic arc opens tenderly at mp, builds through successive phrases with Romantic hairpins to a fortissimo peak around mm.25-28, then broadens and softens into a resolved, glowing D-major close.

sections.label: Phrase A — Statement
sections.notes: Sing the theme espressivo at !mp!, gently tapered dotted phrase-endings; let each 4-bar arch breathe with a soft hairpin.

sections.label: Phrase A' — Violin takes flight
sections.notes: Take the melody at !mf! with warm vibrato and slight lingering at cadences; grow through the phrase with a !p!<!f! hairpin, easing back at m.12.

sections.label: Phrase B — Inner glow
sections.notes: Noble, cantabile at !mf!, sustaining tied notes across barlines; project over the flowing violin arpeggios above chromatic inner suspensions.

sections.label: Phrase C — Cello lyricism
sections.notes: Rich tenor-register singing at !mf!<!f!, expressive rubato at the descending line; let the tone swell into the G-major turn at m.21.

sections.label: Phrase D — Climax
sections.notes: Full-throated !ff! at the high point, broad bow strokes and radiant vibrato; sustain the peak, then begin a slight broadening toward m.30.

sections.label: Coda — Resolution
sections.notes: Ritard and glow: begin !f! then taper the final D6 with a warm !f!>!p! diminuendo, all voices resolving suspensions into a hushed, luminous chord.

Violin 1.instruction: Lead voice at climaxes with soaring espressivo tone, generous vibrato and Romantic hairpins; when accompanying, spin flowing sixteenth-note arpeggios that stay softer than the active melody carrier.

Violin 2.instruction: Provide gently repeated or arpeggiated inner chords with chromatic passing tones and downward-resolving suspensions; always shade under the melody dynamic, breathing with brief rests at phrase ends.

Clarinet.instruction: Open the work with a tender mp statement; elsewhere weave a lyrical chromatic countermelody, never overpowering the current melody carrier.

French Horn.instruction: Sing noble legato lines with sustained ties across barlines; carry the Phrase B melody warmly, and elsewhere offer sustained horn calls and countermelody beneath the leading voice.

Cello.instruction: Anchor the harmony with flowing arpeggiated bass lines and secondary-dominant motion; step into the tenor-register melody for Phrase C with expressive rubato, handing the bass to the French Horn there.
